comments.body:
**Sub-lemma (per-face linear bound).** For each face $F_i$ with vertex set $\{V_j : V_j\in F_i\}$ and any interior point $p$, prove an explicit inequality
$$\operatorname{dist}(p,F_i)\ \le\ \sum_{j:\,V_j\in F_i}\lambda_{ij}\,\operatorname{dist}(p,V_j)$$
with closed-form coefficients $\lambda_{ij}$ expressed through the face/dihedral angles of $T$ at $V_j$.

This is the 3-dimensional analogue of the **Mordell–Barrow lemma** that underlies the classical Erdős–Mordell inequality in the plane. It is NOT a routine corollary of the 2D statement: a face is a triangle (not a segment), so the projection of $p$ onto $F_i$ must be controlled via two angular parameters per face, obtained by projecting $p$ onto the edges of $F_i$ and using the law of cosines inside the face triangle.

Required: state the coefficients $\lambda_{ij}$ explicitly and prove the inequality with no omitted steps, valid for every interior $p$ and every (non-degenerate) tetrahedron.
